text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.67% today after oil prices stabilized following a week of sharp declines driven by peace hopes in the Iran conflict. Last week crude fell hard—Brent briefly dipped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August—as President Trump signaled the conflict might end "fairly soon," easing fears of supply disruptions. Today's modest gain suggests the market found a floor as investors digested those geopolitical developments and US oil settled around $99.64 per barrel.

The stock's broader two-week decline of 7.5% reflects the real headwind facing energy companies when oil prices fall: lower crude prices directly squeeze profit margins on production. Even with Trump administration officials now discussing an end to the Iran tensions, oil traders aren't rushing back in—the gap between US and world oil prices (US at $99.64 versus Brent at $107.03) shows demand concerns persist globally.
